title: Wall Street Moved Into Insurance. Can State Regulators Keep Up?
html:
It was just over a year ago that insurance regulators in Delaware found no significant issues at two life insurers controlled by Mark Walter, a Wall Street billionaire and owner of the Los Angeles Dodgers.

Months later, federal prosecutors started to come to a different conclusion. They collected evidence that those two insurers, Delaware Life and Clear Spring Life, had misclassified billions of dollars in investments with companies affiliated with other parts of Mr. Walter’s vast financial and sports empire, funneling customer money into potentially riskier investments.

Now, prosecutors and securities regulators are trying to determine whether Mr. Walter’s companies broke laws along the way. Amid the scrutiny, he has been selling his stakes in the L.A. Lakers and the British soccer team Chelsea FC, and his two insurers have announced a plan to reduce the level of affiliated investments.

The investigation has analysts, industry executives and lawmakers sorting out another issue: How did the misclassified investments go undetected by Delaware’s insurance examiners?

The answer is crucial because the nation’s 700 life insurers are regulated at the state level. The potential failings in Delaware, where state regulators oversee dozens of life insurers, call into question whether states can keep pace with Wall Street’s growing role in the insurance business.

Ever since the financial crisis of nearly two decades ago, life insurers have forged partnerships with Wall Street as way to expand their businesses. More than 100 of the nation’s life insurance firms are controlled by or linked to a deep-pocketed private equity firm or investment firm. Some of these insurers have begun plowing billions of dollars from customer premiums into the debt being used to finance the construction of A.I. data centers.
summary: Analysts are questioning how regulators missed billions of improperly reported investments at the heart of an investigation into Mark Walter’s companies.
